title: Hazardous Waste (Control of Export, Import and Transit) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Hazardous Waste (Control of Export, Import and Transit) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Basel Convention plastic waste amendments
sections.summary: Basel Convention parties agreed to expand the Convention to cover certain plastic waste categories, effective 1 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Amidst global concerns about the environmental impact of unregulated trade in plastic waste, parties to the Basel Convention agreed last year to expand the scope of the Convention to cover certain categories of plastic waste.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: This extends the PIC procedure to the export of certain non-hazardous plastic waste as well as plastic waste with hazardous characteristics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: However, most clean and homogeneous plastic waste which has been sorted prior to export and is destined for recycling will not be subjected to the PIC procedure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: These amendments to the Basel Convention will take effect on 1 January 2021.

sections.label: HWA Amendment Bill plastic waste
sections.summary: The HWA (Amendment) Bill seeks to expand the scope of HWA to cover transboundary movement of certain plastic waste categories.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The HWA (Amendment) Bill seeks to expand the scope of HWA to cover the transboundary movement of certain categories of plastic waste.

sections.label: Enforcement powers and plastic waste
sections.summary: Clause 6 expands NEA's enforcement powers to vehicles suspected of carrying hazardous or other waste through land checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Clause 6 amends section 30 to expand NEA's enforcement powers to cover vehicles suspected to be carrying hazardous or other waste into or out of Singapore via our land checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The HWA (Amendment) Bill will allow us to enhance our domestic controls and enforcement powers to comply with the new obligations under the Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: At the same time, we recognise that the flow of clean and valuable recyclables can be legitimate and help to support the adoption of a circular economy at the regional and global level.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We will continue to work with the international and regional community to strike a balance between facilitating the legitimate flow of such resources and safeguarding against the unregulated or illegal transboundary movement of waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In fact, in May 2019, the United Nations (UN) estimated that 100 million tonnes of plastic have been dumped in the oceans thus far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Vivid and graphic pictures have become iconic symbols of the impact plastic has had on marine life and have rallied nations around the world to strengthen regulations relating to the global trade in plastic waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill is based on the amendments made to the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal in 2019 to target plastic waste.

sections.label: Plastic waste requiring prior informed consent
sections.summary: Two kinds of plastic waste are subject to prior informed consent: plastic waste mixed with hazardous materials and contaminated recyclable plastic waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Following the changes to the Convention in 2019, two kinds of plastic waste are subject to prior informed consent: plastic waste mixed with hazardous materials, such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles containing pesticides, and plastic waste that can be recycled only after undergoing the cleaning process due to contamination of foreign materials.

sections.label: Economic impact of plastic pollution
sections.summary: The UN Environment Programme estimates the economic impact of plastic pollution on marine ecosystems at at least US$8 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, as the economic impact of plastic pollution on marine ecosystems is estimated by the UN Environment Programme to be at least US$8 billion a year, it would make sense for nations, including Singapore, to work towards reducing plastic pollution, not just by reducing new entrants, but also looking into innovative possibilities to remove what has already entered the marine environment.

sections.label: Plastic production and ocean pollution
sections.summary: Around 100 million tonnes of plastic are in the oceans, and plastic production rose from 2.3 million tonnes in 1950 to 450 million tonnes by 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even though half of all plastics ever manufactured have been made in the last 15 years, there are already around 100 million tonnes of plastic in the oceans, 80% to 90% from land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2019, it was reported in National Geographic that plastic production has increased exponentially, from 2.3 million tonnes in 1950 to 450 million tonnes by 2015 and which is expected to double by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These facts bring to bear the importance of the Bill we are debating today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill, when enacted, will help Singapore fulfil its obligations under the Basel Convention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It will bolster our commitment towards tackling the problem of plastic pollution and reducing the ill-effects of hazardous waste.

sections.label: Singapore plastic waste recycling rates
sections.summary: Singapore recycled 4% of about 950,000 tonnes of plastic waste in 2018, and 96% was not recycled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Singapore recycled a paltry 4% of about 950,000 tonnes of plastic waste in 2018, down from the recycling rate of 6% in 2017, and less than half the rate from five years ago.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With these amendments, we hope to contribute to the efforts to regulate the international trade in contaminated plastic waste.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, only limited types of plastics, such as resin products and specified fluorinated polymers that have been sorted and cleaned, will be exported without restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, it is still very disturbing to note that 96% of the plastic waste we generated has not been recycled, and plastics form the largest category of waste by weight, way ahead of other categories, such as food, paper and cardboard.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Even worse, our plastic waste per capita has been increasing, by about 20% over the last 15 years.

sections.label: Bill on plastic waste flows
sections.summary: The Bill signals Singapore's intention to join the global community in ending plastic waste flows and unsustainable disposal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I am going to use my phone to read the speech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill signals Singapore's intention and resolve to join the global community in ending the flows of plastic waste, and unsustainable consumption and disposal of plastic waste more generally.

sections.label: NEA on recycled plastic trash
sections.summary: According to NEA, only 7% of 40,700 tonnes of recycled plastic trash was processed locally, the rest shipped overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to NEA, only 7% of the 40,700 tonnes of plastic trash that was recycled last year were processed locally and the rest was shipped overseas.

sections.label: Basel Convention Ban Amendment
sections.summary: On 5 December 2019, the Ban Amendment to the Basel Convention enters into force and becomes international law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 5 December 2019, the Ban Amendment to the Basel Convention, a global prohibition on dumping hazardous waste, enters into force almost 25 years after its adoption and officially becomes international law.

sections.label: Ratifying countries' closest neighbours
sections.summary: Countries that have ratified include Singapore's three closest neighbours Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The countries that have ratified include our three closest neighbours Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei.

sections.label: Plastic waste, NEA, Zero Waste Plan
sections.summary: NEA clarified three plastic waste containers were sent back to Singapore as the Malaysian importer lacked permits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just last week, NEA clarified that three containers of plastic waste were sent back to Singapore as the Malaysian importer failed to get permits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This could be both a regional responsibility and opportunity for Singapore, given the need for innovative waste management solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask this noting that the Zero Waste Master Plan issued by the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) last year stated that the Ministry "hope  to promote innovative circular business models and position our companies to seize opportunities in the region for specialised waste treatment, recycling or re-manufacturing." As I conclude, Mr Deputy Speaker, I would like to quote former US Secretary of State John Kerry, at Our Ocean Conference in Bali on 29 October 2018. "In the 1950s and 1960s, what brought me into public life was the nuclear freeze and arms control, the issues of peace… But now, folks, we need to face up to the fact that we've got to treat the issue of the oceans, protection of the oceans, protection of the planet, with the same urgency that we treated arms control and nuclear weapons… we need a non-proliferation treaty for pollution in the oceans." As a state party to the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, we should take note of Article 207(4) of the Convention, which specifically requires states to “endeavour to establish global and regional rules, standards and recommended practices and procedures to prevent, reduce and control pollution of the marine environment from land-based sources”.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A study published in the journal, Nature Climate Change, in May 2019, has estimated that by just converting all plastic manufacturing to fully recycled plastic, we can reduce global greenhouse gas emissions by at least 1.6 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalent by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That would be the equivalent of Japan’s estimated annual greenhouse gas emissions today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should not miss the opportunity to propose this at the next UN Environment Assembly in 2021.

sections.label: Basel Convention plastic waste changes
sections.summary: Changes to the Basel Convention taking effect 1 January 2021 will make it harder for Singapore to export plastic waste for recycling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the changes to the Basel Convention that will take effect on 1 January 2021 will make it harder for Singapore to export our plastic waste for recycling.

sections.label: Semakau landfill lifespan
sections.summary: With more plastic waste, the Semakau landfill could be filled earlier than 2035, its projected end of lifespan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With more plastic waste on our hands, the Semakau landfill could be filled even earlier than 2035, which is the projected end of its lifespan.

sections.label: Plastic waste recycled locally
sections.summary: In 2018, only 7% of the plastic waste Singapore recycled was processed locally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2018, only 7% of the plastic waste that Singapore recycled was processed locally.

sections.label: NEA plastic recycling statistics
sections.summary: NEA's latest statistics showed Singapore recycled 4% of plastic waste, compared to 99% for metals and 56% for paper and cardboard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: NEA's latest statistics showed that we only managed to recycle 4% of our plastic waste, compared to 99% for metals, 56% for paper and cardboard.

sections.label: Basel permits issued since 1996
sections.summary: Since becoming a Party to the Convention in 1996, Singapore has issued an average of 150 Basel permits a year for transboundary waste movement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Since 1996, when we became a Party to the Convention, we have issued an average of 150 Basel permits a year for the transboundary movement of wastes.

sections.label: HWA Act penalties
sections.summary: Under the HWA Act, companies falsely declaring such wastes or exporting them without a valid Basel export permit can be fined up to $300,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Under the HWA Act, companies that falsely declare such wastes, or export such wastes without a valid Basel export permit, can be fined up to $300,000.

sections.label: Singapore plastic waste statistics
sections.summary: In 2018 Singapore generated about 949,000 tonnes of plastic waste, 12% of total waste, and 4% was recycled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2018, approximately 949,000 tonnes of plastic waste were generated in Singapore, which was about 12% of the total waste generated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Four percent of the plastic waste generated was recycled.

sections.label: Packaging waste as priority
sections.summary: Packaging waste was made a priority waste stream in the Zero Waste Masterplan and the Resource Sustainability Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As such, we have made packaging waste a priority waste stream in both the Zero Waste Masterplan and the Resource Sustainability Act.

sections.label: Closing the Waste Loop initiative
sections.summary: The S$45 million Closing the Waste Loop R&D Initiative supports research into new circular economy solutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The S$45 million Closing the Waste Loop R&D Initiative supports research into new circular economy solutions.

sections.label: Resource Sustainability Act introduced
sections.summary: Last year the Resource Sustainability Act was introduced to give effect to a regulatory framework promoting resource sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Last year, we introduced the Resource Sustainability Act, a landmark legislation to give effect to a regulatory framework to promote resource sustainability and support the management of our priority waste streams.

sections.label: Reporting framework and EPR
sections.summary: The mandatory reporting framework will lay the foundation for an Extended Producer Responsibility framework for packaging waste management.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The mandatory reporting framework will also lay the foundation for an Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework for packaging waste management.

sections.label: Citizens' Workgroup on disposables
sections.summary: A Citizens' Workgroup of Singaporeans from diverse backgrounds will be formed to tackle excessive consumption of disposables.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: A Citizens' Workgroup for Singaporeans from diverse backgrounds will be formed to work on measures to tackle the issue of excessive consumption of disposables in Singapore.

sections.label: Microbead entry assessment
sections.summary: NEA assessed that no further measures are needed at this point to manage microbeads entering wastewater and the environment until further scientific evidence emerges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NEA has, therefore, assessed that no further measures are needed at this point to manage the entry of microbeads into our wastewater and into our environment, until further scientific evidence emerges.

sections.label: HWA Amendment Bill compliance
sections.summary: The HWA (Amendment) Bill will enable Singapore to comply with new Basel Convention controls on transboundary movement of certain plastic waste categories.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The HWA (Amendment) Bill will enable Singapore to comply with the new controls on the transboundary movement of certain categories of plastic waste under the Basel Convention.

sections.label: New recycling economic opportunities
sections.summary: It is hoped new economic opportunities will be created for the local recycling industry to seize, creating good jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In doing so, we hope that new economic opportunities will be created that the local recycling industry will seize, which will create good jobs for Singaporeans.
